evals.expected_output: Dispatches document-reader for a proposed concept/relation delta, runs find_concepts per candidate, presents choices via AskUserQuestion across multiple rounds, and only calls research_graph_write after explicit approval for each write.
expectations: Dispatches document-reader rather than fetching/parsing full text itself
Calls find_concepts for every candidate concept before deciding new vs alias vs skip
Uses at least two separate AskUserQuestion rounds (candidate selection, then properties/relation details) before any write
Does not call research_graph_write until the user has approved that specific write
Reports which concepts/edges were actually written, distinct from any declined during review

evals.prompt: What concepts does my note about the RAPTOR paper touch?
evals.expected_output: Reads the note's text directly via research_notes_read rather than dispatching document-reader, proposes concepts/relations grounded in the note's own wording, and checks for any Pointer-to-Pointer references to other documents named in the note.
expectations: Resolves 'my note about the RAPTOR paper' via research_notes_search rather than assuming a note id
Reads the note directly (research_notes_read), not via document-reader, since the source is a note
Considers whether the note's text names another document, proposing a references edge if so
Still runs the full find-or-create and approval flow before any write

evals.prompt: Add the 'gradient checkpointing' concept from this paper, but don't duplicate it if it's already there under a different name.
evals.expected_output: Calls find_concepts('gradient checkpointing'), surfaces a near-duplicate candidate like 'activation checkpointing' if one exists, and asks the user whether to alias onto it rather than creating a new concept.
expectations: Calls find_concepts before create_concept, never creates without checking first
Presents any fuzzy-matched existing concept as an explicit alias-or-new choice via AskUserQuestion
If the user picks alias, calls update_concept adding the new label to aliases, and never overwrites the existing label field
Does not silently decide the match is 'close enough' or 'not close enough' - the user always picks

evals.prompt: Extract concepts from arxiv 2401.99999 — I already extracted from an earlier version of this paper.
evals.expected_output: Runs the normal extraction flow, and if a write raises a metadata_conflict error (e.g. re-touching a concept's metadata with a differing value for an existing key), surfaces the conflicting key(s) and both values via AskUserQuestion (keep existing / use new / merge) rather than letting the raw error reach the user, then re-issues the write.
expectations: Does not present a raw ToolError/metadata_conflict message to the user unhandled
Names the specific conflicting metadata key(s) and both candidate values when asking how to resolve
Re-issues the write with the user's chosen resolution rather than abandoning the write silently
Only proceeds to the next concept/edge after this one is resolved, not in parallel
